input: Sketch out a floor plan for the new home office layout

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether this is a dedicated room, a shared space, or a room conversion determines how much of the layout is fixed vs. flexible and what elements must be included.
The actual room dimensions and shape (including doors, windows, and fixed features like closets or outlets) are the hard physical constraints that drive every placement decision.
Whether one person or multiple people will use the office simultaneously changes how many workstations, seating areas, and storage zones are needed.
The format of the sketch (hand-drawn, digital tool, scaled diagram) and the immediate next action depend on what tools the user has and what they plan to do with the output.
A tight budget or a hard move-in deadline affects whether existing furniture must be reused or new pieces can be purchased, which directly shapes layout options.
Style and functional priorities — e.g., maximising natural light, minimising distractions, standing desk preference — determine how zones and furniture are oriented.
Understanding what the finished plan must achieve (e.g., fits specific equipment, passes a landlord review, guides a contractor) sets the bar for what a good layout looks like.

gold.taskTitle: Sketch a home office floor plan layout
gold.taskDescription: Create a floor plan sketch that maps out the spatial arrangement of furniture, equipment, and zones in the user's new home office.

questions.title: Is this a dedicated room or a shared space?
questions.description: Determine whether the office occupies its own room, shares a space like a bedroom or living area, or is a conversion of another room type.

questions.title: What are the room's dimensions and fixed features?
questions.description: Gather the floor area measurements and note fixed elements such as door and window positions, alcoves, closets, and electrical outlets.

questions.title: How many people will regularly work in this office?
questions.description: Establish whether the layout needs one workstation, multiple desks, or a mix of solo-work and meeting/collaboration space.

questions.title: What format should the finished floor plan be in?
questions.description: Decide whether the output should be a quick hand-drawn sketch, a scaled paper plan, or a digital file using a tool like RoomSketcher or AutoCAD.

questions.title: Must any existing furniture be incorporated into the layout?
questions.description: Identify pieces that must be reused due to budget or preference constraints, as their fixed dimensions will anchor the rest of the arrangement.

questions.title: What working style or atmosphere are you prioritising?
questions.description: Capture key preferences such as maximising natural light, minimising noise, standing-desk use, or a specific aesthetic direction like minimal or industrial.

questions.title: What will this floor plan actually be used for?
questions.description: Clarify the intended use of the plan — personal reference, guiding a furniture purchase, directing movers, or submitting to a contractor or landlord.
